notes: Let k be the integer quotient and suppose k is nonsquare. Choose a positive solution for this fixed k minimizing a+b and arrange a>=b. If b=1, division gives a+1 | 2, hence a=1 and k=1. Thus b>=2 and k>=2. For P(X)=X^2-kbX+b^2-k, the second integral root is a_1=kb-a and aa_1=b^2-k. If k>=b^2, set c=-a_1=a-kb>=0, so ac=k-b^2. If c>0 then ac>=a>kb>=2k>k-b^2=ac, impossible; hence c=0 and k=b^2, contradicting nonsquare. Therefore k<b^2, so a_1>0. Also P(b)=(2-k)b^2-k<0, while P(b)=(b-a)(b-a_1), and a>=b; since P(b)<0, a>b and a_1<b. Thus (a_1,b) is a positive solution with smaller sum, contradiction.
